articles.title: Lula abre série de entrevistas do segundo turno na TV Globo | G1
articles.standfirst: Entrevista faz parte da cobertura do segundo turno das eleições presidenciais de 2026, que terá também conversa com Flávio Bolsonaro e debate entre os candidatos.
articles.summary: A entrevista de Lula na Globo abre a cobertura do segundo turno das Eleições 2026, que terá conversa com Flávio Bolsonaro e o debate presidencial na Globo.
articles.body:
Lula dá entrevista ao JN — Foto: Manuella Mello/Globo

O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) , candidato à reeleição, é entrevistado pela TV Globo nesta quinta-feira (15). A conversa é conduzida pela jornalista Renata Lo Prete e faz parte da cobertura do segundo turno das Eleições 2026 .

A entrevista ocorre ao vivo nos Estúdios Globo, no Rio de Janeiro , e é exibida pela TV Globo, pela GloboNews e pelo g1.

Após a exibição, a entrevista ficará disponível na íntegra no Globoplay e no g1.

Confira os principais temas da entrevista de Lula à Globo

Lula assumiu a responsabilidade por dificuldades enfrentadas pelo seu governo. Questionado sobre o que teria feito de maneira diferente, o presidente afirmou que não poderia atribuir a culpa a outras pessoas.

“Se eu não conseguir ser compreendido pela sociedade brasileira sobre o que o governo faz, eu não posso ficar jogando a culpa em ninguém. Eu tenho que jogar a culpa em mim”, disse.

Lula avaliou que parte das dificuldades enfrentadas por sua gestão esteve relacionada à situação em que encontrou o país ao assumir a Presidência, depois do governo de Jair Bolsonaro (PL). O presidente afirmou que precisou dedicar os primeiros dois anos à recuperação do país e citou o que classificou como desmonte de dez ministérios.

“Eu só lamento que eu não tenha tido a capacidade de fazer o povo compreender as coisas que eu fiz, porque foram muitas coisas”, afirmou.

Outro assunto abordado foi a governabilidade de um eventual próximo mandato do PT diante do novo Congresso: o PL elegeu 121 deputados federais e 19 senadores.

O presidente focou sua resposta nos números da esquerda, afirmando que, para o seu governo atual, foi eleito com 70 deputados e 9 senadores. Segundo ele, com essa composição, conseguiu aprovar “99% de tudo” que fizeram no Congresso, incluindo a reforma tributária.

Lula também disse que, com exceção do PL, todos os partidos participaram do seu governo. “Tivemos uma grande participação das pessoas no governo. É por isso que nós conseguimos aprovar tudo. E se não for assim, você não governa o país”, disse.

Flávio Bolsonaro será entrevistado nesta sexta (16)

Lula abre a série de entrevistas da Globo com os candidatos que disputam a Presidência neste segundo turno das eleições. A ordem das entrevistas foi definida por sorteio em reunião com representantes das campanhas.

O candidato Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), que também disputa o segundo turno da eleição presidencial, será entrevistado na sexta-feira (16), também por Renata Lo Prete.

A entrevista poderá ser acompanhada ao vivo pelos seguintes canais e plataformas:

Globoplay : entrevista completa disponível após a exibição;

g1 : conteúdo na íntegra após a transmissão.

Quando será o debate presidencial da Globo?

No dia 23 de outubro, a TV Globo realizará o último debate entre os candidatos à Presidência da República no segundo turno das Eleições 2026.

Foram convidados Lula (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). O encontro será realizado nos Estúdios Globo, no Rio de Janeiro, e mediado pelo jornalista César Tralli.

O debate será transmitido ao vivo pela TV Globo, com exibição simultânea pela GloboNews e pelo g1, logo após o Jornal Nacional.

articles.title: Lula questiona Flávio sobre 6x1; candidato do PL apresenta ministério | G1
articles.standfirst: Petista voltou a defender que Lula é o único capaz de implantar a redução da jornada de trabalho e criticou o adversário, que teria dito a aliados que reverá a medida caso eleito. Flávio Bolsonaro prometeu ampliar oportunidades de renda e capacitação no novo ministério e apresentou o programa 'ViraPix'.
articles.summary: Lula defende o fim da escala 6x1 sem redução salarial enquanto Flávio Bolsonaro apresenta o Ministério da Prosperidade e o programa ViraPix.
articles.body:
Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula — Foto: REUTERS/Diego Vara e REUTERS/Adriano Machado

A propaganda eleitoral gratuita dos candidatos à Presidência da República desta quinta-feira (15) foi marcada por críticas de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) às posições de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) sobre o fim da escala 6x1 e, do lado do candidato do PL, pela apresentação do Ministério da Prosperidade.

A peça de Lula, a primeira a ser exibida, defendeu o fim da escala 6x1, aprovada na última quarta (14) no Senado, e reforçou que o petista é o único capaz de implantá-la sem a redução do salário.

A propaganda ainda afirma que Flávio Bolsonaro teria mudado de posição sobre o tema após a pressão do presidente e das manifestações populares. A peça diz que Flávio pretende rever e derrubar a proposta caso o candidato do PL seja eleito .

Em outro trecho, a propaganda petista retomou críticas ao adversário do PL relacionadas ao Banco Master. O programa também questionou a atuação de Flávio ao longo de sua trajetória política.

Já o programa de Flávio Bolsonaro foi dedicado à apresentação do Ministério da Prosperidade, que o candidato pretende criar, se eleito.

A proposta prevê ações de capacitação profissional, acesso a crédito e incentivo ao empreendedorismo. Flávio afirmou que, sob a atuação do ministério, o Bolsa Família será mantido e fortalecido.

Segundo Flávio, a pasta teria como objetivo ampliar as oportunidades para que os brasileiros aumentem a renda, estudem, abram negócios e conquistem autonomia financeira. A criação do ministério, no entanto, não está prevista no plano de governo registrado pelo candidato do PL na Justiça Eleitoral. No documento, Flávio propõe o corte de, no mínimo, dez pastas do governo.

A peça também apresentou o 'ViraPix', iniciativa que, segundo Flávio, devolverá aos consumidores parte do dinheiro gasto em pagamentos, incluindo despesas como contas de luz e prestações. A propaganda não detalhou como a proposta seria implementada. A iniciativa também não consta no plano de governo registrado pelo candidato no Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE).

A propaganda do candidato do PL também voltou a explorar as manifestações pró-Lula realizadas no domingo (11), em São Paulo, exibindo imagens da depredação de uma estação do metrô durante o ato.

articles.title: Transporte coletivo: Lula diz que vai enviar ao Congresso PEC para garantir tarifa zero aos finais de semana com dinheiro de emendas | G1
articles.standfirst: Proposta prevê tarifa zero em todas as cidades do país. Proposta foi anunciada pelo presidente em uma publicação nas redes sociais a 10 dias do segundo turno das eleições.
articles.summary: Proposta prevê tarifa zero em todas as cidades do país. Proposta foi anunciada pelo presidente em uma publicação nas redes sociais a 10 dias do segundo turno das eleições.
articles.body:
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) afirmou que vai enviar ao Congresso Nacional uma Proposta de Emenda a Constituição (PEC) que prevê tarifa zero para ônibus aos finais de semana em todo o país.

Em uma publicação nas redes sociais, o presidente afirmou que a fonte de recurso da medida será por compartilhamento de emendas parlamentares.

"Agora que o Senado aprovou o fim da escala 6x1 e os trabalhadores terão dois dias de descanso para ter lazer, visitar família, passear e descansar mais, vou mandar uma PEC também para o Congresso Nacional garantindo passe livre no final de semana para todas as cidades que tiverem transporte coletivo nesse país", disse o presidente.

"E aonde vamos arranjar dinheiro? Aí nós vamos compartilhar com as emendas parlamentares para a gente poder garantir que o povo vai passear. O povo vai ficar feliz, deputados vão dar utilidade para suas emendas e a gente vai garantir que valeu a pena o fim da escala 6x1".

Uma proposta de emenda à Constituição (PEC) passa por uma tramitação mais rígida que a de um projeto de lei comum.

🔎Para ser aprovada, precisa ser analisada pela Câmara e pelo Senado, com votação em dois turnos em cada Casa, e obter, em cada votação, o apoio de três quintos dos parlamentares: 308 dos 513 deputados e 49 dos 81 senadores.

Se Câmara e Senado aprovarem o mesmo texto, a emenda é promulgada pelas Mesas das duas Casas, sem necessidade de sanção do presidente da República; se o Senado alterar o texto aprovado pelos deputados, ou vice-versa, a parte modificada precisa voltar à Casa anterior para nova análise.

Usuário utiliza a tarifa zero aos domingos na cidade de São Paulo. — Foto: Leon Rodrigues/SECOM/PMSP/Divulgação

Nos últimos dias, reta final para a votação do segundo turno, o presidente Lula tem anunciado novas medidas populares voltadas para trabalhadores e estudantes.

Na terça-feira (13), Lula anunciou o perdão das dívidas de todos os microempreendedores individuais - os MEIs - que estão inscritos na dívida ativa da União e um pix de até R$ 5 mil por beneficiário, sem necessidade de devolução, para investimentos nos pequenos negócios.

Um dia depois, a Câmara aprovou as medidas anunciadas pelo candidato petista , que inclui também a ampliação do limite de faturamento para enquadramento de MEI.

O presidente afirmou que o pagamento será de R$ 700 durante dez meses e no final de cada ano de curso, depósito em poupança de R$ 2,5 mil.

Nesta quarta-feira (14), o Senado aprovou a PEC que acaba com a escala 6x1 e garante dois dias de folga por semana para o trabalhador sem diminuição do salário.

A aprovação da PEC por ampla maioria foi uma vitória para o presidente Lula (PT), que transformou o tema em bandeira de campanha. A expectativa é que a proposta seja promulgada no Senado no início da semana que vem. Segundo a campanha de Lula, o petista deve comparecer à cerimônia na Casa legislativa.

Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) — Foto: Ricardo Stuckert

articles.title: Maioridade penal: racha no governo trava PEC da Segurança no Senado | G1
articles.standfirst: Votação está prevista para essa quinta-feira, mas líderes de Lula ainda desenham estratégia depois de oposição querer diminuir maioridade para 14 anos.
articles.summary: Líderes do governo Lula divergem sobre a redução da maioridade penal na PEC da Segurança, enquanto a oposição pressiona por punições a partir dos 14 anos.
articles.body:
Os líderes do governo do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) no Senado Federal se dividiram sobre a proposta do senador Camilo Santana (PT-CE) de incluir na PEC da Segurança Pública a diminuição da maioridade penal para 16 anos em crimes hediondos.

Apesar da ideia de Camilo neutralizar a proposta que colocaria adolescentes mais jovens em risco de prisão, parte do PT é contra incluir a alteração nesse momento.

Integrantes do partido dizem que é preciso discutir isso com mais calma por ser uma mudança importante na lei penal. Historicamente, a bancada do PT no Congresso Nacional se posicionou contra a redução da maioridade penal.

A divisão segue mesmo com o início da sessão do Senado desta quinta-feira (15), na qual a PEC da Segurança deveria ter sido o primeiro item analisado.

Com o impasse, o presidente da Casa, senador Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), decidiu votar primeiro o projeto de lei que aumenta o teto de faturamento do MEI (Microempreendedores Individuais).

Plenário do Senado Federal — Foto: Jonas Pereira/Agência Senado

O racha entre governistas começou na manhã desta quinta. Ainda que sem acordo com os demais colegas de partido, Camilo conseguiu assinaturas necessárias para apresentar a emenda e o fez logo antes do início da sessão.

A proposta do ex-ministro da Educação é para reduzir a maioridade penal para 16 anos em casos de crimes hediondos. O restante dos crimes manteria a idade de responsabilização criminal aos 18 anos.

Já na quarta-feira (14), integrantes do PL apresentaram emenda para reduzir a maioridade para 14 anos em casos hediondos e 16 para todos os demais.

A expectativa dos senadores é de um acordo para que a PEC da Segurança Pública possa ser promulgada na próxima semana e o presidente Lula possa anunciar a criação do Ministério da Segurança Pública.

Caso algum trecho sobre maioridade seja aprovado e o texto precise voltar para a Câmara para aprovação dos deputados, governistas falam em fatiar a PEC:

a parte que já foi aprovada por deputados e senadores segue para promulgação; e

as partes que precisam de análise dos deputados (maioridade penal) é enviada à Câmara como um texto separado.

No novo comunicado, os bispos reafirmam o conteúdo de uma carta enviada aos parlamentares em junho. Para a CNBB, "a redução da maioridade penal não enfrenta as causas da violência nem oferece respostas duradouras para a segurança pública".

A carta é assinada pelo Conselho Permanente da CNBB, que inclui o presidente, os dois vice-presidentes e o secretário-geral da entidade.

O texto afirma ainda que "o Brasil será mais seguro se investir na proteção, na educação e na promoção de sua juventude, e não ampliando o encarceramento precoce de adolescentes”.

articles.title: Senado adia votação da PEC da Segurança Pública por falta de acordo no governo sobre a redução da maioridade penal | G1
articles.standfirst: A PEC aumenta a participação do governo federal nas ações de combate às organizações criminosas.
articles.summary: A PEC aumenta a participação do governo federal nas ações de combate às organizações criminosas.
articles.body:
O Senado adiou a votação da PEC da Segurança Pública por falta de acordo no governo sobre a redução da maioridade penal.

A sessão foi convocada pelo presidente do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre , do União Brasil , a pedido do governo. O Palácio do Planalto orientou os senadores governistas a concluir a votação nesta quinta-feira (15), a dez dias da eleição.

A PEC aumenta a participação do governo federal nas ações de combate às organizações criminosas. Cria, por exemplo, o Sistema Único de Segurança Pública, o Susp, que vai integrar a atuação das forças de segurança da União, estados e municípios; e prevê punições mais severas aos chefes de facções e sem direito à progressão de pena nem às saídas temporárias, as saidinhas.

A oposição anunciou que votaria a favor, mas apresentou uma emenda que reduz a maioridade penal para 16 anos, para a maioria dos crimes, e para 14 no caso de crimes hediondos, como tráfico de drogas e homicídio. Na tentativa de diminuir o impacto da estratégia da oposição, o líder do PT no Senado, Camilo Santana, apresentou uma outra emenda, com a redução da maioridade para 16 anos, mas só para crimes hediondos.

Senado adia votação da PEC da Segurança Pública por falta de acordo no governo sobre a redução da maioridade penal — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

No plenário, o líder do PL, senador Carlos Portinho, pediu que a emenda do governo fosse obrigatoriamente votada, o que poderia levar o texto de volta para a Câmara:

“Na medida em que o PT convergiu com o interesse em redução da maioridade penal”, diz o senador Carlos Portinho, PL – RJ.

Mas, pouco depois, Alcolumbre decidiu retirar a PEC da Segurança da pauta:

“Eu estou sendo o culpado de emendas que foram apresentadas, de que vai alterar o texto, voltar para a Câmara e que não pode ser uma discussão açodada”.

O senador Camilo Santana disse que o governo tem pressa na votação:

"E queria fazer um apelo, Sr. Presidente Alcolumbre, para que a gente possa, o mais rápido possível, votar essa PEC aqui neste Senado".

Senadores da oposição criticaram o adiamento da votação. Governistas estão divididos sobre a própria emenda que reduz a maioridade penal. Uma alternativa seria enviar uma proposta separada sobre o tema. Mas ainda não há acordo.

articles.title: Enamed obrigatório: Câmara aprova 'OAB da Medicina' para médicos | G1
articles.standfirst: Obtenção de nível proficiente no resultado final será requisito para o exercício da profissão. Texto segue ao Senado e precisa ser votado até esta sexta para não perder validade.
articles.summary: O Enamed obrigatório exigirá nível proficiente para o exercício da medicina após aprovação da Câmara, com o texto seguindo para votação urgente no Senado.
articles.body:
A Câmara dos Deputados aprovou nesta quinta-feira (15) a proposta que estabelece novas diretrizes para a aplicação do Exame Nacional de Avaliação da Formação Médica (Enamed). Entre as novas regras, estão a exigência de uma nota mínima e a aplicação da prova em três períodos do curso de medicina.

O projeto é resultado de uma medida provisória editada pelo governo Lula em junho e segue para análise do Senado . O texto precisa ser votado até esta sexta-feira para não perder validade e seguir à sanção presidencial.

Os médicos graduados com diploma reconhecido nacionalmente e obtido antes da publicação da medida provisória, em 19 de junho de 2026, não serão submetidos ao Enamed.

O Enamed já existe desde 2025 e era utilizado para avaliar a qualidade dos cursos de medicina e selecionar candidatos para programas de residência médica.

Agora, passa a ter também a função de verificar se o formando atingiu o desempenho mínimo considerado necessário para atuar como médico.

O relator da medida provisória, deputado Doutor Luizinho ( PP -RJ), propôs que a prova seja aplicadaem três momentos durante o curso:

A terceira prova terá peso maior em relação às avaliações anteriores.

Os pesos e as pontuações mínimas serão determinados pela Comissão Nacional de Avaliação da Formação Médica, que será criada pelo Ministério da Educação e terá integrantes do próprio MEC, do Ministério da Saúde e do Conselho Federal de Medicina (CFM).

Os integrantes da Comissão serão trocados a cada dois anos e a presidência do colegiado será alternada entre os representantes indicados pelo governo e pelo CFM.

articles.title: Desentendimento no PT ajudou a adiar votação da PEC da Segurança, diz José Guimarães | G1
articles.standfirst: Ministro responsável pela articulação política afirmou que "oposição percebeu a fragilidade" do partido e ajudou a suspender a sessão.
articles.summary: Ministro responsável pela articulação política afirmou que "oposição percebeu a fragilidade" do partido e ajudou a suspender a sessão.
articles.body:
O ministro da Secretaria de Relações Institucionais (SRI), José Guimarães, afirmou nesta quinta-feira (15) que a retirada de pauta da votação Proposta de Emeda à Constituição (PEC) da Segurança Pública ocorreu após um "desentendimento" dentro da bancada do PT e que a "oposição percebeu a fragilidade" do partido e ajudou a suspender a sessão.

A votação estava prevista para esta sessão, mas, ao adiar a votação, o presidente do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP) mencionou a falta de um entendimento sobre emendas apresentadas ao texto que alteram a maioridade penal.

Ao g1, o ministro responsável articulação política do governo disse que o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) havia dado uma orientação para a bancada no Senado para que a votação da PEC ocorresse sem nenhuma emenda e que as emendas que existiam da oposição e do governo deveriam tramitar em PEC paralela, o que não ocorreu.

"Houve um desentendimento, existia uma orientação, pelo que fui informado pelo relator da matéria, Rogério Carvalho, do presidente da República de orientar hoje pela manhã a discussão e votação da PEC sem nenhuma emenda".

"E as emendas que existiam, tanto do Rogério Marinho, como do senador Camilo, iriam tramitar em PEC paralela, não misturar os assuntos com a PEC da Segurança, o que foi aprovado na Câmara, aprovado na CCJ do Senado. Houve essa confusão e essa confusão acabou paralisando a votação, a oposição percebeu a fragilidade na unidade do PT e terminou ajudando a oposição ajudando na suspensão da sessão", disse Guimarães.

José Guimarães, líder do governo na Câmara — Foto: Lula Marques/Agência Brasil

Líderes do governo Lula ainda desenham uma estratégia para lidar com o tema após a oposição querer incluir no texto a diminuição da maioridade penal para 14 anos.

O senador Camilo Santana (PT-CE), um dos coordenadores da campanha pela reeleição do presidente, apresentou uma emenda com o objetivo de diminuir a maioridade para 16 anos em crimes hediondos.

Interlocutores do presidente do Senado afirmam que a retirada de pauta ocorreu porque nem o governo nem a oposição teriam votos suficientes para aprovar suas as emendas – e o cálculo, neste caso, seria de deixar o assunto para depois.

Guimarães afirmou ainda que a discussão sobre a redução da maioridade penal tem que ser feita, "mas não em apenas um dia só".

"Vamos botar essa discussão dentro da PEC, que aliás abordamos na Câmara, tem uma PEC tramitando lá que trata do tema, nós vamos discutir na hora certa e não misturar alhos com bugalhos. Essa é a posição do governo".

Apesar da ideia de Camilo neutralizar a proposta que colocaria adolescentes mais jovens em risco de prisão, parte do PT é contra incluir a alteração nesse momento.

Integrantes do partido dizem que é preciso discutir isso com mais calma por ser uma mudança importante na lei penal. Historicamente, a bancada do PT no Congresso Nacional se posicionou contra a redução da maioridade penal.

O racha entre os integrantes do partico começou na manhã desta quinta. Ainda que sem acordo com o restando dos colegas de bancada, Camilo conseguiu assinaturas necessárias para apresentar a emenda e o fez logo antes do início da sessão.

A proposta do ex-ministro da Educação prevê reduzir a maioridade penal para 16 anos em casos de crimes hediondos. O restante dos crimes manteria a idade de responsabilização criminal aos 18 anos.

O senador Jaques Wagner (PT-BA) disse que o governo não pediu o adiamento, mas que não houve acordo com a oposição sobre o tema ser colocado em uma PEC paralela. Ele não descartou que a PEC da Segurança seja votada na próxima semana.

articles.title: Universidade conclui apuração do 'ranking' sexual com fotos de alunas  | G1
articles.standfirst: Comunicado feito pela Universidade do Oeste Paulista foi divulgado nesta quinta-feira (15) e mencionou a suspensão e expulsão de envolvidos na exposição indevida de alunas do curso de Psicologia.
articles.summary: A Universidade do Oeste Paulista (Unoeste) concluiu a apuração interna sobre um “ranking” sexual feito com fotos de alunas em Presidente Prudente (SP).
articles.body:
Polícia Civil investiga suposto ranking sexual com fotos de estudantes de universidade em Presidente Prudente (SP) — Foto: Redes Sociais/Reprodução

A Universidade do Oeste Paulista (Unoeste) concluiu a apuração interna sobre um “ranking” sexual feito com fotos de alunas em Presidente Prudente (SP). O comunicado foi divulgado nesta quinta-feira (15).

Conforme a Unoeste, a sindicância foi instaurada para apuração do ocorrido, envolvendo a exposição indevida de acadêmicas do curso de Psicologia. O crime foi denunciado por alunas em 20 de agosto deste ano.

A instituição não informou quantos estudantes foram punidos e afirmou que adotou as medidas cabíveis assim que tomou conhecimento dos fatos.

A Polícia Civil também cumpriu um mandado de busca e apreensão contra um dos investigados. Ao todo, 44 vítimas foram identificadas. Destas, 24 já prestaram depoimento , 11 têm oitivas agendadas e nove aguardavam o cumprimento de cartas precatórias.

A Unoeste informou que a apuração foi conduzida por uma comissão responsável, que analisou individualmente as condutas e seguiu as normas institucionais, garantindo o direito de defesa dos envolvidos e os demais procedimentos previstos.

Ao fim da investigação, a universidade aplicou sanções administrativas de acordo com a responsabilidade de cada aluno. As penalidades variaram de suspensão à expulsão.

Além disso, a Unoeste disse que seguirá promovendo ações de orientação, prevenção e acolhimento, reforçando seu compromisso com um ambiente acadêmico seguro, respeitoso e responsável.

Em Presidente Prudente (SP), alunas de uma universidade privada foram expostas e avaliadas em um “ranking” sexual compartilhado em um grupo fechado de um aplicativo de mensagens. O conteúdo foi vazado e expôs mensagens de teor sexual e depreciativo, gerando uma investigação da Polícia Civil . O caso foi divulgado em agosto.

As fotos das estudantes foram retiradas das redes sociais sem autorização e distribuídas no aplicativo de mensagens. As imagens eram acompanhadas de comentários ofensivos e classificações com termos como "deliciosíssima", "comível" e "arrebentaria".

No grupo de mensagens, diversos alunos faziam comentários a respeito do "ranking". "Tirei as lésbicas e as gordas", disse um deles. "Tem umas aí que eu discordo", apontou outro.

O caso, que foi registrado na Delegacia de Defesa da Mulher (DDM), provocou protestos com faixas e cartazes em frente à universidade, localizada às margens da Rodovia Raposo Tavares (SP-270). O coletivo “Frente pela Vida das Mulheres” emitiu uma nota de repúdio ao episódio, classificado como “ um ato de misoginia organizada ”.

“É algo nojento, esdrúxulo. [...] A gente fica completamente sem chão”, desabafou uma das universitárias que teve a imagem exposta . A jovem estava sozinha quando descobriu e ficou se sentindo desamparada.

articles.title: Redução da maioridade penal: oposição tenta incluir na PEC da Segurança | G1
articles.standfirst: Emenda quer idade penal de 16 anos para a maioria dos crimes e de 14 para crimes graves. A regra atual, de 18 anos, está na Constituição desde 1988; no período colonial, crianças podiam ser punidas a partir dos 7.
articles.summary: A PEC da Segurança propõe reduzir a maioridade penal para 16 anos, retomando um debate histórico sobre a idade mínima para punição criminal no Brasil.
articles.body:
O plenário do Senado deve votar nesta quinta-feira (15) a PEC da Segurança Pública, e a oposição vai tentar usar a sessão para incluir na proposta a redução da maioridade penal. O tema não está no texto aprovado pela Câmara, versão que a Comissão de Constituição e Justiça (CCJ) do Senado manteve ao concluir a análise da PEC na quarta (14).

A mudança consta de uma emenda apresentada na quarta pelo senador Rogério Marinho ( PL -RN) e assinada também pelo senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), candidato à Presidência. Como a CCJ não incorporou a sugestão, a oposição pretende levá-la a voto em separado no plenário, por meio de um destaque. A emenda de Marinho fixa a maioridade penal em 16 anos para a maior parte dos crimes e 14 anos para crimes hediondos, tortura, tráfico de drogas, terrorismo, organização criminosa e associação criminosa, entre outros.

O líder do PT no Senado, Camilo Santana (CE), apresentou uma sugestão de alteração à PEC que reduz a maioridade penal para 16 anos em casos de crimes hediondos. A proposta, mais restrita, é uma resposta à emenda de Marinho e também está em jogo na sessão desta quinta.

O calendário eleitoral pesa sobre a votação, que acontece na reta final do segundo turno da disputa presidencial. Pesquisa Quaest divulgada na quarta aponta a redução da maioridade penal entre as propostas mais bem avaliadas pelos eleitores .

O debate recoloca em discussão uma questão que acompanha a história da legislação brasileira há mais de dois séculos. Ao longo do tempo, a idade para responsabilização criminal já foi fixada em 7, 8, 9, 14 e, desde 1940, 18 anos.

Menores infratores comentam a redução da maioridade penal — Foto: Glauco Araújo/G1

Período colonial: punição a partir dos 7 anos

Quando Dom João VI chegou ao Brasil, em 1808, valiam as Ordenações Filipinas. Com base no Direito Canônico, que situava a chamada "idade da razão" por volta dos 7 anos, a responsabilização penal começava nessa idade.

Quem tinha entre 7 e 17 anos não podia ser condenado à morte, mas estava sujeito a outras penas e ficava preso nos mesmos lugares que os adultos. Para jovens de 17 a 20 anos, a pena podia ser reduzida em até um terço.

Nas Ordenações Filipinas, pessoas entre sete e dezessete anos não eram condenadas à pena de morte mas podiam sofrer outras punições — Foto: Reprodução

O Código Criminal do Império, de 1830, adotou o sistema de discernimento e fixou a maioridade penal absoluta em 14 anos. Mesmo assim, crianças a partir dos 8 anos podiam ser responsabilizadas se o juiz concluísse que haviam agido com consciência do ato, e a punição podia chegar, em casos extremos, à prisão perpétua. Menores de 17 anos iam para casas de correção, prisões em que a pena era cumprida com trabalho.

Trecho do Código Criminal do Império (1830). — Foto: Reprodução

1890: redução e subjetividade na República

Com o Código Penal Republicano de 1890, ninguém com menos de 9 anos podia ser punido. Entre 9 e 14 anos, voltava a caber ao juiz avaliar o discernimento.

Pelo artigo 30 do código, os que tivessem agido com discernimento seriam recolhidos a "estabelecimentos disciplinares industriais" pelo tempo definido pelo juiz, desde que não passassem dos 17 anos.

1921 e 1927: Primeiras leis específicas para menores

No início do século 20, a imprensa já publicava estatísticas sobre a prisão de crianças e adolescentes, e juristas como o desembargador Nabucco de Abreu defendiam a criação de um juízo especializado em menores, argumentando que a legislação da época era insuficiente para lidar com as especificidades da infância e adolescência. Na época, o tema já era tratado pela imprensa com dados e estatísticas sobre a prisão de crianças e adolescentes.

Em 1920, infrações atribuídas a crianças e adolescentes já ganhavam destaque no noticiário — Foto: Kayan Albertin - Arte/g1

A Lei Orçamentária nº 4.242, de 1921, introduziu conceitos como abandono e perda do pátrio poder (hoje, destituição do poder familiar) e determinou que menores de 14 anos não seriam submetidos a nenhum tipo de processo penal.

Trecho da Lei Orçamentária de 1921 — Foto: Reprodução/Senado Federal

Em 1927, o primeiro Código de Menores da América Latina trocou a lógica puramente punitiva pela da educação e da regeneração, e elevou a idade de irresponsabilidade penal para 14 anos.

1940 até hoje: o critério biológico e os 18 anos

O Código Penal de 1940 adotou o critério biológico, em vigor até hoje: menores de 18 anos passaram a ser considerados penalmente inimputáveis por ainda estarem em desenvolvimento físico, mental e emocional.

Em 1969, durante a ditadura militar, o Decreto-Lei nº 1.004 tentou reintroduzir o critério do discernimento, permitindo punir jovens de 16 a 18 anos que compreendessem o caráter ilícito de seus atos. A regra nunca chegou a produzir efeitos e foi revogada em 1978.

Da doutrina da situação irregular à proteção integral

O Código de Menores de 1979 seguia a Doutrina da Situação Irregular, que autorizava o Estado a intervir na vida de menores de 18 anos considerados abandonados, carentes, em risco ou autores de atos infracionais, com caráter sobretudo assistencial e tutelar.

A Constituição de 1988 consolidou a inimputabilidade dos menores de 18 anos no artigo 228, que os submete a legislação especial. Em 1990, o Estatuto da Criança e do Adolescente (ECA) substituiu o Código de Menores e adotou a doutrina da proteção integral. O ECA considera criança quem tem até 12 anos incompletos e adolescente quem tem de 12 a 18 anos. Em vez de penas, prevê medidas socioeducativas, como advertência, liberdade assistida e internação.

Segundo Marinho, punir adolescentes é necessário para evitar que eles sejam recrutados pelo crime organizado. Flávio Bolsonaro defendeu a proposta na quarta, durante agenda de campanha em Porto Alegre, citando a idade de 16 anos como regra e de 14 anos para crimes graves, como estupro.

A bancada do governo no Congresso é contra. Os governistas argumentam que a mudança pode agravar a situação do sistema prisional e expor jovens mandados a presídios à influência de facções. Há também uma objeção jurídica: na análise de outra PEC sobre o tema na Câmara, deputados governistas sustentaram que a redução atingiria direitos e garantias fundamentais protegidos pela Constituição.

Para Rafael Cardozo, juiz de direito do Tribunal de Justiça de Pernambuco e presidente do Fórum Nacional da Justiça Juvenil (FONAJUV) as regras atuais para a responsabilização de crianças e adolescentes que cometem atos infracionais são referência, e não um "afrouxamento da resposta do Estado".

"Na verdade, o que houve foi uma mudança de paradigma. O adolescente, aquele com 12 anos completos e 18 anos incompletos, passou a ser sujeito de direitos e a ser reconhecido como pessoa em desenvolvimento".

Segundo o juiz, a responsabilização precisa existir, mas de forma compatível com a condição de pessoa em desenvolvimento. "Não é uma escolha entre punir ou proteger. Na verdade, o sistema socioeducativo ele foi desenhado para responsabilizar o adolescente, mas protegendo" , explica Cardozo.

De acordo com Mariana Araújo, coordenadora do Centro de Defesa da Criança e do Adolescente do Ceará (CEDEC) e representante da Coalizão pela Socioeducação, a promulgação da Constituição de 88 e a criação do ECA, sob influencia da Convenção dos Direitos da Criança da ONU de 89 dão "respostas ao histórico de violações que crianças e adolescentes sofreram ao longo dos anos".

Mariana pontua que esses marcos definiram que crianças e adolescentes devem ter, tanto da sociedade como da família e do Estado, a proteção integral.

"A partir dessa visão é de que o artigo 227 da Constituição e o 228, eles estabelecem que a população de 12 a 18 anos deve ter um outro tipo de tratamento pelo cometimento de ato infracional. Então, estabelece um outro sistema de responsabilização."

articles.title: FBI probes suspicious white powder letters sent to Schumer, Dem senators as threat spreads nationwide
articles.summary: Senior Capitol Hill staff were warned about suspicious letters containing unknown substances mailed to multiple congressional offices and election offices nationwide.
articles.body: Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., and two other Senate Democrats were the intended recipients of mail that federal investigators say contained "suspicious substances," Fox News Digital has learned. A source familiar confirmed to Fox News Digital that Schumer's office was the intended target, among other congressional offices, of a mysterious envelope containing an unknown substance. He wasn't the only Senate Democrat targeted. Sens. Chris Murphy, D-Conn., and Alex Padilla, D-Calif., were both informed by the FBI that their respective offices were sent a suspicious letter on Thursday, following warnings in both chambers of Congress that federal investigators were "investigating multiple letters containing suspicious substances that were mailed to various addresses nationwide, including multiple Congressional offices." Josh Sorbe, a spokesperson for Murphy, told Fox News Digital that the senator’s office "was sent a letter with a suspicious substance." ARMED MAN ARRESTED AT US CAPITOL BARRICADE AS POLICE PROBE WHY HE DROVE ONTO RESTRICTED GROUNDS "Our office was promptly informed of the letter by FBI, SAA, and Capitol Police, and we continue to work closely with them and federal law enforcement," Sorbe said. "Due to those efforts and various safety protocols, the Senator and staff were not in immediate danger. Our office is grateful for the investigators involved in this incident, and we intend to continue close coordination as the investigation continues." A spokesperson for Padilla told Fox News Digital, "We received the notification from the FBI that one of our offices was mailed a letter containing a suspicious substance, but it was intercepted by USPS." The two incidents follow warnings sent out to top-ranking staff on the Hill earlier Thursday by both the Senate and House sergeants at arms that the FBI, U.S. Postal Inspection Service, and U.S. Capitol Police were actively investigating the matter, per notices obtained by Fox News Digital. DEPROGRAMMED: FORMER DSA INSIDER REVEALS ‘FRIGHTENING’ SOCIALIST AGENDA DROVE HIM FROM ‘EXTREME’ IDEOLOGY "Law enforcement officials are working to intercept any additional letters before they are delivered, however, it is possible that some letters may reach their destinations," the notice from the Senate Sergeant at Arms read. The exact nature of the suspicious substances, and just how many congressional offices are intended recipients, remains unclear. Top staff in the House were warned by the House Sergeant at Arms that the office had "been made aware of reports of letters containing suspicious white powder substances received by public officials throughout the United States." "Although no House Members have been identified as intended recipients at this time, the SAA continues to monitor the situation and coordinate with law enforcement partners," the notice read. "All offices are reminded to remain vigilant and follow safe mail handling procedures to help protect staff from potentially harmful materials." An FBI spokesperson declined to confirm specific instances or letters, but said in a statement that, "The FBI and U.S. Postal Inspection Service are investigating a series of suspicious mailings sent to various addresses nationwide, including Secretary of State offices and their related election offices." "Some of the letters contained an unknown substance, and we are working closely with our law enforcement partners to respond to each incident," the spokesperson said. "We are also working with our partners to identify the individual or individuals responsible for the letters. This FBI and the U.S. Postal Inspection Service will continue to safeguard the public and secure elections for American citizens." MASSIVE TROVE OF REPUBLICAN VOTER AND DONOR INFO BREACHED IN BIDEN DOJ PROBE: SENATE CHAIRMAN Included in the Senate Sergeant at Arms' notice was an image of one of the envelopes that included a return address in the top-left corner for the Democratic Socialists of America’s (DSA) headquarters in New York City. It is unclear whether the DSA had any involvement in sending the letters. Fox News Digital reached out to the DSA for comment but has not heard back.A representative for the organization told the New York Post that the DSA "has not occupied this office address since 2013." "We are also no longer headquartered at 75 Maiden Lane," the rep said. The notice warned that "all suspicious letters, packages, or substances should be treated as potentially hazardous." Suspicious letters were also sent to state elections offices around the country. The National Association of Secretaries of State and the National Association of State Election Directors said in a joint statement that, "Those who administer our elections should never fear for their safety while carrying out their essential duties." "Election officials take these matters seriously and work closely with law enforcement and security partners to protect their personnel and facilities," the organizations said. "We have security measures and contingency plans in place to respond to potential threats and emergencies while maintaining essential election operations." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP It comes on the 25-year anniversary after an anthrax-laced letter was opened by a staffer in then-Senate Majority Leader Tom Daschle’s office on Oct. 15, 2001. Since then, Congress has drastically overhauled how it accepts mail. Packages and mail no longer come directly to the Hill, and instead are processed in facilities where they are screened and irradiated before making their way to a congressional office.

articles.title: America's next war could reach US soil, top Army general warns
articles.summary: The Army's new "How the Army Fights" framework prepares American forces for contested deployments as drones and surveillance reshape the battlefield.
articles.body: The American military has largely operated on a familiar premise: combat the enemy overseas before the fight reaches home. But as drones, cyberattacks and long-range weapons pose growing threats to U.S. military installations and critical infrastructure, Army leaders are preparing for a future in which American forces could come under attack before they ever deploy overseas. "If we're going against a pacing threat, power projection will be contested," Gen. Christopher LaNeve, the Army's acting chief of staff, told Fox News Digital on Wednesday. He said the military is rethinking assumptions that were held during decades of fighting in Iraq and Afghanistan, when American forces could largely count on secure bases and supply lines at home. FBI WARNS BATTLEFIELD-STYLE DRONE ATTACKS COULD REACH US: 'ONLY A MATTER OF TIME' "During the Global War on Terror, we took a lot of things for granted, because we could," LaNeve said during a small-group roundtable at the Association of the United States Army's annual conference in Washington this week. In a potential conflict with China, disrupting American military bases, transportation networks and communications could delay U.S. forces from reaching the battlefield. The Pentagon's latest report on China's military capabilities warns that Beijing has positioned cyber capabilities inside U.S. critical infrastructure networks that could be used to disrupt American military mobilization during a conflict. The concerns come as the Pentagon places renewed emphasis on homeland defense and military installations as they prepare to potentially confront threats closer to home. U.S. officials have previously confirmed drone incursions over installations — including Joint Base Langley-Eustis in Virginia and Picatinny Arsenal in New Jersey. Though those incidents have not been publicly attributed to China. The warning of a future fight on American soil comes amid the How the Army Fights rollout. The new operational framework places greater emphasis on preparing American forces to deploy, communicate and sustain operations even when military bases, supply lines and communications networks are under attack. The guidance places greater emphasis on the Army's ability to deploy and sustain forces under threat, including when communications, supply lines and military infrastructure are disrupted. US MILITARY BASES ARE ‘ILL-EQUIPPED’ TO STOP DRONE SWARMS, TOP COMMANDER REVEALS AFTER RUBIO'S UAP WARNING LaNeve said the Army is using the framework to establish clearer priorities for how its formations train, fight and incorporate new technology. "It was important to get this document out to provide a direction for our Army, a stake in the ground in where we're moving," LaNeve told Fox News Digital in an interview Wednesday. The changes are being led by an Army leadership team serving in acting capacities following the departures of former Army Secretary Dan Driscoll and Chief of Staff Gen. Randy George. LaNeve remains the Senate-confirmed vice chief of staff. LaNeve explained how the Army is preparing to keep fighting even when an adversary disrupts military communications. "I think what you would see inside this command and control capability is the ability to operate disconnected and then reconnect when you have that capability, but to continue to be able to maneuver," he said. The Army is also rethinking how it protects military installations at home. LaNeve pointed to Joint Interagency Task Force 401, which is working with federal and local law enforcement to strengthen counter-drone defenses around military bases and critical infrastructure. CARTELS USE DRONES TO SCOUT BORDER AGENTS AND MAP SMUGGLING ROUTES, EXPERT WARNS Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle pointed to the southern border as an example of how soldiers are already confronting drone threats closer to home. He said soldiers are using the mission to test new counter-drone technology against real-world threats, gaining experience they can bring back to their units as the Army prepares for future conflicts. The Army is also expanding its preparations for biological threats that could disrupt military operations. Officials announced this week that biological incidents will be incorporated into routine combat training as part of a broader effort to ensure soldiers can continue carrying out their missions through disease outbreaks or deliberate biological attacks. During a separate panel Wednesday, Air Force Secretary Troy Meink warned that advances in surveillance technology could soon make it increasingly difficult for military forces to operate anywhere without being detected. "We are rapidly heading to a point in time where, depending on what your signature is, how fast you're moving, the enemy is going to have some sense to where you are no matter where you are on the planet," Meink said. He suggested that level of surveillance could emerge within five years, potentially sooner, as China and other adversaries expand their ability to track and target military assets. Meink said the Pentagon is working to make its forces more survivable, including through autonomous systems capable of operating in dangerous environments where commanders might hesitate to send manned platforms. War Secretary Pete Hegseth, speaking alongside Meink and the other service secretaries, criticized what he described as the Pentagon's failure to keep pace with technological advances under the Biden administration. "On hypersonics, they took a nap. On space, they took a nap. On weaponization of space, they took a nap. On drones, they took a nap," Hegseth said. LaNeve emphasized that despite the Army's growing reliance on advanced technology, soldiers must still be able to carry out their missions when those systems are unavailable. "Soldiers are our number one platform. It is the Army's platform," he told Fox News Digital. articles.title: Poll: Democrats favorable to socialism, have no idea how to pay for it
articles.summary: To anyone who says they have a favorable view of socialism, but they’d be really mad if the government went to so far as to raise their taxes: Just you wait and see what the new crop of elected Democratic legislators are going to do.
articles.body:
Every now and then, a poll or a chart really encapsulates the entire problem we face as a country. According to a survey by the Economic Innovation Group, Democrats have a net favorable view of socialism by 31 points. Yes, socialism. The economic system of the old Soviet Union, and Cuba, and North Korea — of so many dictatorships over the last 100 years that have starved and oppressed their people.

How on earth could any American political constituency have favorable view of that?

At the same time, according to this exact same survey, Democrats, like Republicans, independents, young people, old people and every survey-able demographic there is, all think taxes are too high .

Moderate liberal commentator Matthew Yglesias describes this as the “strange evolution” of the modern Democratic Party, but to some extent it just describes Americans in general: A lot of people want a more robust welfare state, but they have no idea how to pay for it — and in fact, they already think they pay too much.

Leftist influencers and media figures have tried to solve this dilemma by gaslighting their supporters into thinking that we generate much more spending, even with lower taxes on most people, if we just raise taxes on the very wealthiest Americans. Confiscate more wealth from Elon Musk, that sort of thing. The problem with this plan is that it would not work at all. It is a fantasy that we can balance the budget that way. The very rich already pay an overwhelming share of the taxes. There’s just not that much more to squeeze.

As the economist Jessica Riedl notes: “Self-described socialists expect taxes on the super-wealthy to finance all of socialism. Its not a theory of shared sacrifice as much as lazy free lunch economics. And politicians feed that by promising free lunches.”

And yes, the politicians are to blame. They’re always guaranteeing more stuff but they don’t actually want to raise taxes on seniors, who receive most of the government benefits. At best, or at worst, they’ll support increases on income taxes and property taxes for younger Americans because these people don’t vote.

By the way, none of this is actually socialism. To be honest, I don’t even believe most Democrats who say they have a positive view of socialism actually know what it is. All too many people seem to believe that socialism just means the government spends more money on health and education and welfare. That is not socialism. You can be a vigorously capitalist country and still spend lots of money on welfare, that’s just most of northern Europe.

Socialism is an economic system in which the workers seize the control of the means of production, which in practice means that a powerful central government directs all the resources in society, ostensibly on behalf of the workers. Under socialist systems, entrenched and unaccountable government bureaucracies decide which factories produce which goods, who to trade with, how much food you get, all of those sorts of things. It’s an interesting idea, and it never ever ever works, because without a functioning free market, where firms compete to offer goods and services at the most effective price that people are willing to pay, you actually can’t calculate prices at all, so nobody knows how to value one good over another, and the result is mass poverty.

It would be a very, very, very bad to enact this system, and frankly it doesn’t seem like most self-described socialists at the ground level even want to do it.

At the elite level, however, the members of the Democratic Socialists of America, the DSA, which is currently taking over the party, actually does want to implement real socialism, or something similar to it. Their agenda calls for abolishing market capitalism and overturning the Constitution. It’s dangerous and radical, and it’s exactly what people like Angie Nixon and Claire Valdez and Darializa Avila Chevalier will try to accomplish when they get into Congress.

So to anyone who says they have a favorable view of socialism, but they’d be really mad if the government went to so far as to raise their taxes: Just you wait and see what the new crop of elected Democratic legislators are going to do. You won’t like it very much!

Robby Soave is co-host of The Hill’s commentary show “Rising” and a senior editor for Reason Magazine. This column is an edited transcription of his daily commentary.

articles.title: Trump to campaign in Iowa twice before Election Day
articles.summary: Jeff Kaufmann, chair of the Iowa Republican Party, said Thursday that President Trump will campaign in the Hawkeye State twice before Election Day. “I just got off the phone with President Trump. He told me that he will be in Iowa on October 22 and November 1. He is anxious for Iowans to hear his…
articles.body:
Jeff Kaufmann, chair of the Iowa Republican Party, said Thursday that President Trump will campaign in the Hawkeye State twice before Election Day.

“I just got off the phone with President Trump. He told me that he will be in Iowa on October 22 and November 1. He is anxious for Iowans to hear his message before they vote. Stay tuned for further details,” Kaufmann wrote on social media.

The announced stops come as the prospect of Democrats flipping an Iowa Senate seat becomes increasingly likely.

A Marist poll released Thursday showed Democratic state Rep. Josh Turek leading Rep. Ashley Hinson (R-Iowa) 48 percent to 45 percent among likely voters in Iowa. Turek’s lead fell within the poll’s 6.6 percent margin of error.

However, an Emerson College poll released last week showed Hinson leading Turek 47 percent to 45 percent among likely voters. That lead is also within the poll’s margin of error of 3.8 percent.

The nonpartisan Cook Political Report rates Iowa’s Senate race as a “toss-up,” but according to Decision Desk HQ , Hinson is narrowly seen as the favorite to win the race.

The last time a Democrat from Iowa was elected to the Senate was in 2008.

articles.title: FBI employees involved in Trump classified documents case sue over ‘unlawful’ firings
articles.summary: Nine former FBI employees involved in the classified documents case against President Donald Trump filed suit Thursday against FBI Director Kash Patel and Attorney General Todd Blanche, alleging their firings were “unlawful.”
articles.body: Nine former FBI employees involved in the classified documents case against President Donald Trump filed suit Thursday against FBI Director Kash Patel and Attorney General Todd Blanche, alleging their firings were “unlawful.” The group’s suit says they were fired without cause for their work on the case involving Trump, and that the firings appeared to be politically motivated. It noted they were booted while Patel was being criticized by the administration for partying with the U.S. Olympic hockey team. FBI Special Agent Miles Starr, who was working in a unit called the “Director’s Advisory Team” that was apparently formed to look into Trump’s perceived political enemies, had demanded urgent access to the “Plasmic Echo” case file — the code name for the investigation into the classified documents case — on Feb. 23, the lawsuit says. That was after video of Patel chugging a beer and “flinging alcohol around the U.S. men’s hockey team’s locker room at the Winter Olympics in Milan, Italy, began circulating widely on social media and news sites,” the suit says. The file had the names of the agents who’d worked on the investigation, and they were summarily fired over the next few days without any of the required due process, the suit says. “Each Plaintiff was provided with a termination letter signed by Director Patel” that falsely claimed that they had exercised “poor judgment and a lack of impartiality in carrying out their duties, leading to the political weaponization of the government,” the suit says. Patel later told Congress they were fired for cause and after internal investigations, claims the suit says are not true. NBC News has reached out to the FBI and the Justice Department for comment. The filing says the former employees “did not volunteer to participate in Plasmic Echo; they were assigned to the case because they were members of specific FBI Counterintelligence and Intelligence squads” and the nine “performed their duties apolitically.” Among the other cases members of the group had worked on were the Boston Marathon bombing and the investigation into the attempted assassination of Trump in Butler, Pennsylvania. The plaintiffs, Jennifer Bacon, Zach Feldman, Gilbert Granados, Catherine Herrera, Harrison Kaufman, Jeremy Linton, Erin Matanic, Danielle Ray and Rachel Vaccaro, have “over a century of experience and service to the FBI” among them and were “involved in numerous high-profile investigations to thwart threats and respond to crises and attacks against the United States,” the suit says, and their abrupt firings affected more than just them. The nine were “involved in ongoing and sensitive counterintelligence and counterterrorism investigations in connection with threats emanating from countries across the globe,” the filing says. “As a result of their unlawful and hasty firings, Plaintiffs’ investigations were not properly transferred to other FBI Special Agents or Analysts,” it says. “The impacts of these heedless actions on America’s national security is immeasurable.” The group’s attorneys, Margaret Donovan, Abbe D. Lowell and Rebecca S. Tinio, said in a joint statement that the suit would prove their clients were unlawfully fired and hold the Trump administration accountable for “this blatant attack on the rule of law.” The agents were dismissed “because they did their jobs, as they always did, to follow the facts and law without bias or favor. To this administration, this is an offense. To the rest of us, it is heroic,” the lawyers’ statement said. The agents’ investigation helped lead to the then-former president being charged in June 2023 on allegations that he lied and schemed to mislead federal investigators to retain sensitive materials that he knew were still classified after he left the White House. The indictment alleged that the documents he took with him “included information regarding defense and weapons capabilities of both the U.S. and foreign countries; United States nuclear programs; potential vulnerabilities of the United States and its allies to military attack; and plans for a possible retaliation in response to a foreign attack.” Trump was later charged with trying to obstruct the investigation. He pleaded not guilty to all the charges, and the case was ultimately dismissed after U.S. District Judge Aileen Cannon, a Trump appointee, found the special counsel who led the investigation, Jack Smith, had been appointed improperly. A Justice Department appeal of that ruling was dropped after Trump was re-elected in 2024. The lawsuit says it was clear that employees who’d worked on investigations involving Trump were “doomed” because he and other top government officials “made clear in numerous public statements that they intended to exact revenge against anyone Trump deemed to have wronged him.” “Before and after Plaintiffs’ firings, President Trump, Defendant Patel, Defendant Blanche, and others in Trump’s orbit publicly impugned Plaintiffs’ integrity, despite their unimpeachable service records; smeared their work as politically motivated, when it was not; and made clear that their fate was sealed by virtue of simply having worked on an investigation into Trump’s wrongdoing,” the complaint reads. The lawsuit notes Starr, the person who accessed the case file, was also involved in the first indictment of FBI Director James Comey last year, a case that was ultimately dismissed and that Comey’s team has said was politically motivated. The suit seeks to have the employees reinstated to their jobs and awarded back pay for the time they’ve missed. A similar lawsuit was filed earlier this year by two former FBI special agents who said they were wrongfully fired for what they described as their minimal roles in “Arctic Frost,” Smith’s investigation into the alleged criminal conspiracy to overturn Trump’s 2020 election loss. Trump pleaded not guilty to the charges in that case, which were dismissed after his election victory due to long-standing Justice Department policy stating that sitting presidents can’t face federal charges. The Justice Department has moved to dismiss that lawsuit, which is pending.

articles.title: Megyn Kelly: Don Lemon should run for president
articles.summary: Former Fox News host Megyn Kelly said she thinks independent journalist Don Lemon should run for president after he teased launching a 2028 bid. During a Tuesday episode of her YouTube show, Kelly referred to Lemon’s Oct. 3 appearance on the podcast “Uncloseted,” where he said the odds he might launch a presidential bid were…
articles.body:
Former Fox News host Megyn Kelly said she thinks independent journalist Don Lemon should run for president after he teased launching a 2028 bid .

During a Tuesday episode of her YouTube show , Kelly referred to Lemon’s Oct. 3 appearance on the podcast “Uncloseted,” where he said the odds he might launch a presidential bid were around “65, 70” percent.

“OK, I’m going to shock you,” Kelly said. “I think he should do it. I actually think he should do it. First of all, it’s not a dealbreaker that he has spent his life as a journalist. I mean, you could absolutely parlay that into a career in public service.”

Kelly took a dig at former President Biden and former Vice President Kamala Harris before asking viewers if they think the pair is smarter than Lemon, later adding she believes the former CNN host “could match wits against” Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.).

“I know [Harris] was at least a lawyer, she was an attorney general for the state of California –– no, I don’t believe so,” Kelly said. “Do you think Joe Biden was? I don’t. Are we so enamored with our public officials now we don’t think somebody like Don Lemon could do it? Honestly, I’m not.”

Kelly said that a Lemon candidacy would give reporters “lots to talk about.”

“I encourage him and I’m rooting for him. He doesn’t actually think he’s going to win, however,” she continued before playing a clip of Lemon on “Uncloseted” in which he talked about the prospect of being the first Black and gay president.

In the clip, Lemon added that he thinks the U.S. is ready for such a candidate, but perhaps not leading into 2028.

The pundit told “Uncloseted” host Spencer Macnaughton that some viewers had asked him about pursuing elected office, specifically about running for president. Lemon said while there’s “a lot on my plate right now,” the feedback people gave him was “very humbling.”

“If the people want me, I’ll do it,” he said last week. “But it is a daunting undertaking to run for president in this country because you’d have to be devoted to it full time. And I would like to devote much of my time to journalism.”

Lemon started his YouTube series, “The Don Lemon Show,” after CNN fired him in 2023. He has been an outspoken critic of President Trump for years.

Earlier this year, he was indicted on federal civil rights and conspiracy charges in connection with his reporting on a protest against Immigration and Customs Enforcement at a Minnesota church.

Among a long roster of diplomats, lawyers, generals, lawmakers and some celebrities to be elected president, former Presidents Warren G. Harding and John F. Kennedy were the only two commanders in chief with careers in journalism, Business Insider reported in July.

Harding was the editor and publisher of The Marion Star, which he purchased for $300 in 1884, while Kennedy was a foreign correspondent for Hearst Newspapers during World War II.

articles.title: White House laughs off 'beclowned' Jimmy Kimmel after crude personal jabs at new press secretary
articles.summary: Jimmy Kimmel called new press secretary Katie Zacharia "Malibu Katie" and mocked her intelligence in two monologues, prompting a fierce White House response.
articles.body: Late-night host Jimmy Kimmel used back-to-back monologues this week to deliver a series of personal insults directed at newly appointed White House press secretary Katie Zacharia, prompting a scathing response from the White House. During Tuesday's episode of ABC’s "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" after Zacharia's first White House press briefing, the comedian called her "Malibu Katie" and mocked her intelligence. "I want to introduce you to the new kid in Trump land. It was the first day of kindergarten for the new White House press secretary, Katie Zacharia," Kimmel said. TRUMP'S NEW PRESS SECRETARY FACES FIRST MAJOR TEST AS WHITE HOUSE BRIEFING ROOM ENTERS NEW ERA Kimmel also suggested Zacharia was appointed to keep President Donald Trump "awake and interested," saying that "every six months they bring in a new fawning blonde dolt to add to the rotation." "Things did not get off to a great start for Malibu Katie today," he continued. "Her first briefing was brief. It was only 14 minutes long. But even in that short time, she accomplished exactly what she was brought in to do, which is slobber a whole tube of lip gloss all over the president's behind." The White House responded to Kimmel's monologues in statements to Fox News Digital. "Jimmy Kimmel is a no-talent loser who has beclowned himself with tanking ratings and by spewing disgusting lies to his dwindling audience," White House spokesman Davis Ingle said. "He is so devoid of actual talent that nobody with any common sense would ever watch him unless it was to laugh at his miserable failures." WHITE HOUSE URGES SITCOM PRODUCER CHUCK LORRE TO SEEK 'PSYCHIATRIC HELP' AFTER HE TARGETED TRUMP, FIRST LADY White House communications director Steven Cheung also defended the new press secretary, praising her qualifications in a statement to Fox News Digital in response to Kimmel's attacks. "Katie is a fabulous and wonderful addition to the team. She is uniquely qualified and whip-smart to help inform the American people about all the great things President Trump and his administration have been doing, and she will do an incredible job as press secretary," Cheung told Fox News Digital. Tuesday marked Kimmel's second consecutive night of mocking Zacharia. On Monday, before her first briefing, the host displayed a gym selfie of Zacharia wearing workout gear while joking about her intelligence. KATIE ZACHARIA HITS GROUND RUNNING, PROMISES TRUMP DIESEL DEAL DELIVERS CHEAPER GAS FOR AMERICANS "This is the new press secretary, former Newsmax commentator Katie Zacharia, seen here, thinking," Kimmel said. He added that her qualifications for the role were having "blonde hair" and being able to "do a thumbs up." Zacharia held her first official White House press briefing Tuesday, days after Trump announced her appointment on Friday. She previously served as a senior communications advisor to Trump Media & Technology Group, which operates the Truth Social platform. "She has an unblemished record of support, and has been a loyal and brilliant supporter, right from the beginning. She is, likewise, a devoted fan and member of MAGA!" Trump wrote. "I am confident that Katie will deliver strong results for our Country as the next White House Press Secretary, as she has the respect of, and will work fantastically with, the Media, the American People, and my Administration." KAROLINE LEAVITT JOINS FOX NEWS AS CONTRIBUTOR AFTER LEAVING WHITE HOUSE PRESS SECRETARY ROLE CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The New York Times described Zacharia's first briefing as a "bumpy debut." During the 14-minute session, she referred to her husband, Tyler Zacharia, as "my president" before immediately correcting herself.

articles.title: MAGA donor hits Guilfoyle, attorneys with defamation lawsuit
articles.summary: Eric Deters, the donor to President Trump whom former U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle reportedly asked to wire $100,000 to her American Express account, leading to her ousting from the Trump administration, sued her and her lawyers for defamation. Deters filed the lawsuit against Guilfoyle and defense attorneys Jesse Binnal and David M. Schwartz…
articles.body:
Eric Deters, the donor to President Trump whom former U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle reportedly asked to wire $100,000 to her American Express account, leading to her ousting from the Trump administration, sued her and her lawyers for defamation.

Deters filed the lawsuit against Guilfoyle and defense attorneys Jesse Binnal and David M. Schwartz in Kenton Circuit Court in Kentucky. He called for them to be charged on one count of defamation, one count of false light invasion of privacy and one additional count against Guilfoyle for breach of contract.

The donor requested damages and a trial by jury.

Deters wrote in the suit that he was notified by the Wall Street Journal’s Dana Mattioli that the ambassador and her legal team told Mattioli that the text exchanges were “false” and that Deters was a “known blackmailer.”

“The texts are not fake. I have never been accused of or charged with blackmail … This statement contains the falsehood that I owed Kim Guilfoyle money,” he wrote.

Mattioli was one of the reporters to publish the Journal’s story about Guilfoyle and the texts to Deters last week.

Guilfoyle denied allegations that she asked Deters to pay off a credit card bill. However, she was asked to resign on Tuesday. New White House press secretary Katie Zacharia started her first press briefing sharing that the Trump administration asked Guilfoyle to resign.

She said after she resigned that she would “not allow false accusations to define my decades of public service,” noting that she would “vigorously” defend herself.

Deters warned Monday on CNN that he planned to sue , telling Anderson Cooper that it’s “going to be fun.”

“They first said that the text messages were fake –– defamation,” Deters told Cooper. “Then they said I was a known blackmailer. I’ve never blackmailed anybody in my life.”

He had told the Journal that he paid Guilfoyle $300,000 over several years to speak at Freedom Fest, a conservative Kentucky-based event he launched in 2020 in opposition to COVID-19 mandates. Deters told Cooper that the diplomat never mentioned an outstanding debt in their text exchanges.

“Now, they’re claiming that there are invoices when she knows that’s not true. In all the text messages, she doesn’t mention anything about me owing money,” he said. “She knows that is phony, and I’m going to be suing them all for defamation.”

Text messages obtained by NewsNation , The Hill’s broadcast partner, showed Guilfoyle appearing to plead to Deters not to share any details about their “arrangement” and warned him he could “literally cost me my ambassadorship.”

Trump said he did not “like what we were reading” when asked about Guilfoyle’s ousting on Tuesday.

The incident was a stunning rebuke of a high-profile Trump ally who was previously engaged with the president’s eldest son, Donald Trump Jr., before the two broke off the engagement in 2024.

“She wasn’t a member of my family,” the president told reporters. I guess she dated my son a long time ago. She was doing a good job, but we didn’t like what we were reading.”

articles.title: RFK Jr.-aligned MAHA group spends big on Iowa governor’s race
articles.summary: A political action committee associated with Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s “Make America Healthy Again” (MAHA) movement announced Thursday it is investing more than $1 million in the Iowa governor’s race — the group’s largest contribution to date. MAHA Action PAC, a federal super PAC run by Kennedy ally and…
articles.body:
A political action committee associated with Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s “Make America Healthy Again” (MAHA) movement announced Thursday it is investing more than $1 million in the Iowa governor’s race — the group’s largest contribution to date.

MAHA Action PAC, a federal super PAC run by Kennedy ally and book publisher Tony Lyons, said it is donating $1.5 million to Republican Zach Lahn’s gubernatorial campaign.

MAHA PAC, a related federal hybrid super PAC, is also deploying $150,000 in independent expenditures in support of Lahn.

Lahn, who describes himself as a regenerative farmer and business owner, made waves during the state’s GOP primary by defeating Rep. Randy Feenstra, an established politician who was endorsed by President Trump.

The Iowa gubernatorial candidate embraces the MAHA mantle, frequently criticizing “Big Agriculture” and the use of toxic pesticides that can contaminate the food supply. His platform includes breaking up farming monopolies and defending smaller, independent farms.

“MAHA was the first to believe in Zach Lahn, and the Iowa Republicans proved us right,” Lyons said in a statement. “The primary showed this movement can nominate. November is where we prove it can win. Our $1.65 million donation is the down payment on the nation’s first MAHA governorship, and we are asking every American who believes in health freedom to help us finish the job.”

Lahn’s Democratic opponent, Rob Sand, also espouses MAHA messages about improving children’s health, clean water and the state’s high cancer rate. Sand is leading Lahn in the polls, with nonpartisan election forecaster Decision Desk HQ projecting the race will “lean” Democrat as of Thursday morning.

MAHA PAC is also planning a 15-day “get out the vote” door-knocking program for Lahn, running from Oct. 21 through the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

While some MAHA grassroots activists think the movement’s key principles should be nonpartisan, its leaders have aligned themselves with Trump and parts of the Republican Party. There have been months of infighting over the movement’s campaign strategy.

MAHA’s political leaders have been working to show the White House that its outreach will pay dividends. If the MAHA coalition can be counted on as a reliable conservative voting bloc in November and keep Republicans in power, Trump may prioritize more of Kennedy’s agenda.

To that end, MAHA PAC said Thursday it will spend $250,000 to support incumbent GOP Reps. Anna Paulina Luna in Florida and Tom Barrett in Michigan, as well as Rep. Kevin Kiley, a former Republican-turned-Independent in California.

The PAC is also spending to support Republican House candidates Brandon Herrera and Jace Yarbrough in Texas, as well as Joe Mitchell in Iowa.

Among the six candidates, Luna, Barrett, Herrera and Mitchell are in competitive races that could determine control of the lower chamber.

articles.title: Lawmakers ‘horrified’ by mass shooting plot on Chicago-area Hindu temple
articles.summary: Several lawmakers have expressed shock and outrage about an alleged racially motivated two-year plot to massacre people at a Hindu temple in Aurora, Ill., which led to the arrest of a 19-year-old Palatine, Ill., man. Alexandros Paporakis was arrested Sunday at an apartment he shares with his mother in the 1300 block of North Baldwin Court…
articles.body:
Several lawmakers have expressed shock and outrage about an alleged racially motivated two-year plot to massacre people at a Hindu temple in Aurora, Ill., which led to the arrest of a 19-year-old Palatine, Ill., man.

Alexandros Paporakis was arrested Sunday at an apartment he shares with his mother in the 1300 block of North Baldwin Court in Palatine.

According to authorities, Paporakis had been planning for two years to commit a mass shooting at Aurora’s largest Hindu temple. On Sunday, he told one of his Taco Bell coworkers he was at a temple, but his gun had jammed and he was on his way to fix it. The coworker called 911, following which authorities located Paporakis and made the arrest.

He is facing several felony charges, including making terroristic threats.

Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-Ill.) wrote on social media Thursday that he and his family were worshipping at the temple in Aurora on Sunday where the mass shooting was supposedly going to happen.

“I’m grateful to those who helped prevent a tragedy, but we must come together to confront the hatred that put so many innocent lives at risk,” Krishnamoorthi wrote in a post on the social platform X.

In a statement attached to his post, Krishnamoorthi added, “This is where the poison of anti-Indian hatred and white supremacy can lead, and we cannot wait until innocent people are killed to take it seriously” and that “every American deserves to live and worship without fear, and we must stand together against hatred in all its forms.”

Authorities said Paporakis had sent an eight-page manifesto to his coworker describing his hate by using racially charged slurs for a variety of non-white people. In the same manifesto he said he planned to kill as many people as possible before taking his own life and shared pictures of a rifle, rifle magazines, body armor and other tactical equipment.

Police found at his home a rifle, multiple loaded rifle magazines, hundreds of rounds of additional rifle ammunition, tactical equipment, a tactical vest containing body armor and a patch with imagery associated with white supremacist extremism.

In a social media post Thursday morning, Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-Md.) said Americans are “outraged” by this mass shooting plot in the Chicago-area temple.

“We must stand together—and strong—against white supremacist hate and violence targeted at temples, synagogues, churches and mosques,” he wrote on X. “When houses of worship are under attack, all Americans must stand up for freedom and equal rights.”

“Today, my heart is with the Aurora community,” the congressman added.

Rep. Rich McCormick (R-Ga.) in a post on X said the “plot to massacre innocent Americans at a Hindu temple is unequivocally wrong.”

“The freedom to worship without fear is a fundamental American right,” he wrote. “Religious hatred, persecution, and violence have no place in our nation.”

A judge ordered Paporakis’s detention Wednesday after he appeared for a hearing. His next court appearance is scheduled for Oct. 30 at 9 a.m.

articles.title: Judge tosses Brennan suit demanding preservation of records in ‘grand conspiracy’ probe
articles.summary: A federal judge on Thursday agreed to toss a lawsuit from former CIA Director John Brennan, arguing he did not yet have standing to sue over an investigation targeting him for his role in reviewing the 2016 election. Brennan brought the suit in July, seeking to compel the Department of Justice (DOJ) to preserve records…
articles.body:
A federal judge on Thursday agreed to toss a lawsuit from former CIA Director John Brennan, arguing he did not yet have standing to sue over an investigation targeting him for his role in reviewing the 2016 election.

Brennan brought the suit in July, seeking to compel the Department of Justice (DOJ) to preserve records related to the investigation, saying they would be needed for an expected vindictive prosecution filing if an indictment was brought.

But U.S. District Judge Jia Cobb said the matter was not yet ripe, agreeing with the Trump administration to toss the suit.

“To have standing to seek forward-looking relief, a plaintiff must allege an injury that is ‘imminent,’ rather than one that is ‘conjectural or hypothetical,’” Cobb wrote.

The judge went on to call it “speculative whether Defendants are deleting records relevant to a future vindictive- or selective-prosecution defense.”

Still, Cobb offered up some scrutiny of her own on the investigation into Brennan, part of the so-called grand conspiracy probing a number of topics, including the past criminal investigations into President Trump.

“Unsurprisingly, Brennan does not believe that he has committed any crime. Much more surprising are Brennan’s allegations regarding DOJ officials who have not found otherwise, despite their alleged marching orders,” Cobb wrote, referencing one former member of the team who determined “that ‘the case against Director Brennan was too weak to bring.’”

She also noted the resignation of Joseph diGenova, who was later tapped to lead the conspiracy probe.

“Joseph diGenova—who had previously made public statements calling Brennan ‘evil’ and a ‘traitor,’ and had declared that the Grand Conspiracy ‘began with John Brennan and ends with John Brennan,’ —reportedly resigned from his position investigating Brennan’s cases and stated ‘if you want indictments where there’s no evidence, you have an ethical problem,’” Cobb wrote.

“One might think that these statements would lead to the termination of the investigations. Instead, Brennan alleges, it has led to the termination of the investigators.”
